extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when an application is considered abandoned (expressly or by failure to act), who may effect abandonment, examiner handling of abandonments, and the procedural requirements and standards for petitions to withdraw a holding of abandonment or to revive an abandoned application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is removed from the Office docket of pending applications either by (A) formal abandonment (expressed by applicant, by attorney/agent of record, or by a registered attorney/agent acting under 37 CFR 1.34(a) when filing a continuing application) or (B) failure of applicant to take appropriate action within a specified time at some stage in prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an applicant formally abandons an application and there is a corporate assignee, the acquiescence must be made through an officer whose official position is indicated. The MPEP treats express abandonments as acts of deliberation; care should be exercised that abandonments reflect the desires and best interests of the applicant and that the correct application is identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express/formal abandonment — who may sign and effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: An express abandonment must be signed by the applicant (acquiesced in by an assignee of record) or by the attorney/agent of record; it becomes effective when an appropriate official of the Office takes action thereon. The date of abandonment may be the date of recognition or another date specified in the letter if so stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorneys/agents must exercise every precaution to ensure abandonment is in accordance with applicant wishes and that the proper application is identified. Action recognizing an express abandonment may be an examiner acknowledgment or Publishing Division receipt. Filing of a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d) or a file-wrapper continuing application under former 1.62(g) is considered a request to expressly abandon the prior application as of the continuing application's filing date. Form paragraph 7.88 may be used to acknowledge proper express abandonments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment compliance (improper express abandonment)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a letter expressly abandoning the application does not comply with 37 CFR 1.138, it is not a proper letter of express abandonment and should be rejected with a fully explanatory letter or acknowledged as improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the letter does not comply, the examiner should use Notice of Abandonment form PTO-1432 (checking appropriate boxes) or send an explanatory letter. Form paragraph 7.89 may be used to acknowledge improper express abandonments. Reasons for noncompliance (e.g., signer not of record) must be fully explained. A letter of express abandonment not timely filed (e.g., outside the period for reply) is not acceptable to expressly abandon; it should be endorsed on the file wrapper and placed in the file but not formally entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment cancelling all claims is not express abandonment (Ex parte Lasscell)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after the filing date that cancels all claims, even if signed by the applicant and assignee, is not an express abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an amendment is regarded as nonresponsive and should not be entered; applicant should be notified as explained in MPEP § 714.03 to § 714.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of appeal may effect abandonment in certain circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney or agent not of record may file a withdrawal of an appeal under 37 CFR 1.34(a), and where such withdrawal would result in abandonment of the application, that withdrawal is in fact an express abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that withdrawal of appeal by non-of-record counsel can operate as abandonment in such instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment after Notice of Allowance — petition to withdraw from issue under 37 CFR 1.313
rubrics_metrics.description: If a letter of express abandonment is submitted in an allowed application, it should be accompanied by a petition to withdraw from issue under 37 CFR 1.313 and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(h). The express abandonment may not be recognized unless received in time to act before the date of issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.313 provides that an allowed application will not be withdrawn from issue except by Commissioner approval and that, after issue fee payment, withdrawal is restricted to specified reasons (including express abandonment). If 37 CFR 1.313 precludes giving effect to an express abandonment, the proper remedy may be a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 showing extraordinary circumstances. Timeliness to avoid publication or issue processing is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to avoid publication by express abandonment (37 CFR 1.138(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.138(c) accompanied by the petition fee may be filed to expressly abandon to avoid publication of the application; the petition should be addressed to Box PGPUB-ABN to increase chances of timely recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition will be granted only if recognized in sufficient time to avoid publication; generally such petitions must be received more than four weeks prior to the projected publication date. A petition filed within four weeks of publication is unlikely to avoid publication. Withdrawal from issue after issue fee payment may not prevent publication under 35 U.S.C. 122(b). See 37 CFR 1.313(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment in interference proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A written declaration of abandonment signed only by an attorney or agent of record, when the application is subject to an interference under 35 U.S.C. 135, is not effective to terminate the interference and will not be considered until ex parte prosecution is resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be effective to terminate an interference proceeding, abandonment must be signed by the inventor with written consent of the assignee where there has been an assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form for filing express abandonment (PTO/SB/24)
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific form (PTO/SB/24) may be used to file an express abandonment under 37 CFR 1.138, including abandonments in favor of a continuing application or to avoid publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the form is reproduced in the MPEP for practitioner use; proper completion and signatures per 37 CFR 1.138 are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to take required action during statutory period (37 CFR 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.135(a) specifies that an application becomes abandoned if applicant 'fails to reply' to an office action within the fixed statutory period; abandonment may also result from insufficiency of reply (failure to file a complete and proper reply within the statutory period per 1.135(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an amendment is filed after expiration of the statutory period, the application is abandoned and the remedy is petition to revive. Examiner should notify applicant using Notice of Abandonment form PTOL-1432; late amendments are endorsed on the file wrapper but not formally entered. Form paragraphs 7.90 and 7.98.02 may be used for notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency of reply and guidance on extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be abandoned where applicant's reply is within the period but not fully responsive to the Office action (insufficiency of reply). Examiners should indicate why reply is not fully responsive and may suggest extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reply appears to be a bona fide attempt with inadvertent omission, use form paragraph 7.95 instead of 7.91. The date on which a petition under 1.136(a) and fee are filed determines the period of extension and corresponding fee. Applicants may not reply outside the six (6) month statutory period or obtain an extension more than five (5) months beyond the date for reply set in an Office action; a fully responsive reply must be timely filed to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special situations that may result in abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain specific procedural situations often give rise to questions of abandonment, including: (A) copying claims from a patent when not suggested by the Office does not constitute a reply; (B) abandonment through withdrawal of or failure to prosecute an appeal to the Board; (C) abandonment through dismissal of appeals to the Federal Circuit or civil action absent a timely responsive amendment; (D) claims suggested for interference near end of period for reply; (E) FWC application under former 1.62; (F) continued prosecution application (CPA) filings; (G) improper RCE filed prior to Board decision that can be treated as withdrawal of appeal; (H) RCE filed without timely submission meeting reply requirements when reply to final action outstanding; (I) allowed application prior to issue fee payment may become abandoned if an RCE is improperly filed without appropriate fee/submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed situation references the relevant MPEP section for further instruction (e.g., §1215.x for appeals, §706.07(h) for RCE treatment). Examiners and applicants should be aware that improper filings (e.g., RCE without required submission/fee) will not toll existing time periods and can cause abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of proceedings under 35 U.S.C. 120
rubrics_metrics.description: Termination of proceedings (for purposes of copendency) occurs when the earlier application is patented, abandoned, or proceedings on it are terminated; 'before' is interpreted as 'not later than.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) failure to pay issue fee results in termination as of the date fee was due; (B) losing an interference as to all claims terminates proceedings as of the date appeal/review was due if no appeal filed; (C) termination after Board decision; (D) termination after court decision. See MPEP § 711.02(c) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration of holding of abandonment versus revival (distinction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may ask for reconsideration of a holding of abandonment if he/she disagrees (e.g., dispute as to sufficiency of reply or controlling dates); primary examiner may reverse a holding as to sufficiency but has no authority to act upon an application where no action was taken during the period for reply (i.e., a reversal that the application was never abandoned is not a revival).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When there is no dispute as to abandonment (cause only), a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 (with fee) is necessary to revive. Where applicant contends application is not abandoned (dates, sufficiency), a petition under 37 CFR 1.181(a) requesting withdrawal of the holding of abandonment is appropriate and does not require a fee. If amendment reached after expiration and dates undisputed, no reconsideration is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to withdraw holding of abandonment under 37 CFR 1.181 — timeliness and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.181 may be filed to withdraw an examiner’s holding of abandonment; 37 CFR 1.181(f) provides that any petition not filed within two months of the mailing date of the action or notice may be dismissed as untimely (the two-month period is generally not extendable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than dismiss an untimely 1.181 petition, the Office may treat it on the merits on condition that, for certain application types (design, pre-June 8, 1995 utility/plant), the petition is accompanied by a terminal disclaimer dedicating to the public a terminal part of patent term equivalent to the period between mail date of notice of abandonment and petition filing. The Office may dismiss petitions showing intentional delay. A granted petition to withdraw the holding results in the application being treated as never abandoned (affecting patent-term extension eligibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive — statutory/regulatory requirements (37 CFR 1.137)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive an abandoned application may be filed on grounds that the delay was unavoidable (1.137(a)) or unintentional (1.137(b)); a grantable petition must be accompanied by the required reply, the applicable petition fee, any required terminal disclaimer and fee, and a showing that the entire delay was unavoidable or a statement that it was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unavoidable petitions (1.137(a)) require a showing to the Commissioner that the entire delay from due date until filing of grantable petition was unavoidable, plus fee per §1.17(l) and any terminal disclaimer required by 1.137(c)/(d). Unintentional petitions (1.137(b)) require a statement the entire delay was unintentional, fee per §1.17(m), and the Commissioner may request additional information. The required reply must be filed (or satisfied by a continuing application or, for post-June 8, 1995 nonprovisional utility/plant apps, by an RCE request in compliance with §1.114). For abandonments for failure to pay issue/publication fees, the reply must include payment of the fee(s). No consideration of petition substance is given until the fee is received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirements when reviving or treating untimely petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to revive in a design application, or in certain utility/plant applications filed before June 8, 1995, must be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer dedicating to the public a terminal part of the term equivalent to the period of abandonment (or limited by 20-year term constraints). Terminal disclaimer must also apply to patents on continuing applications that reference the revived application under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraphs 1.137(d)(1)-(3) specify applicability and exceptions (e.g., not required where revival sought solely for copendency with a post-June 8, 1995 application, to lapsed patents, or to reexamination proceedings). Terminal disclaimers required when office treats untimely petitions on merits to avoid granting patent-term extension for prosecution delay caused by abandonment. Fees for terminal disclaimers are set forth in §1.20(d) and §1.17(l)/(m) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive — acceptable forms of the 'required reply'
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'required reply' for a petition to revive may be filing the substantive reply required to outstanding Office action; in a nonprovisional application abandoned for failure to prosecute the required reply may be met by filing a continuing application; for nonprovisional utility/plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995, the required reply may also be met by filing a request for continued examination (RCE) in compliance with §1.114; for abandonment for failure to pay issue/publication fee the reply must include payment of those fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the proper form of reply is used for the application type and abandonment cause; filing the reply alone is insufficient without the petition and fee where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to withdraw holding of abandonment based on nonreceipt of Office action — required showing
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish nonreceipt of an Office communication and obtain withdrawal of a holding of abandonment, the practitioner must submit a statement that the Office communication was not received and attest that a search of the file jacket and docket records indicates nonreceipt, and attach a copy of the docket record showing where the communication would have been entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office modified the required showing to minimize burdens: submit practitioner's statement plus a docket report showing replies docketed for the expected reply date as documentary proof of nonreceipt (see Notice 'Withdrawing the Holding of Abandonment When Office Actions Are Not Received'). This showing may be insufficient where circumstances suggest the action was lost after receipt (e.g., practitioner history of not receiving Office actions). Court precedent (Delgar v. Schulyer) supports remailing where adequately supported. Evidence of nonreceipt (e.g., Notice of Allowance not received) should be documented; the MPEP gives examples of the documentary proof expected.
